question: An employee says she works ‘for the government’ in Victoria. Can I assume the federal public service pension guide applies when I send her a link?
generated_answer:
No. The federal public service pension guide applies to employees of the federal public service. Employees in the public service of the provinces and territories are subject to the pension plans of their respective public service, and the pension information on this website does not apply to them. You should refer the employee to her employer for pension information. Can I assume that all employees are covered by the public service pension plan? No. Not all employees are eligible for coverage under the public service pension plan. To determine whether an employee is eligible for coverage under the public service pension plan, you need to refer to the employee’s departmental or agency-specific terms and conditions of employment. I am a casual employee. Is there a pension guide for casual employees? The public service pension guide applies to employees who are eligible for membership in the public service pension plan. Casual employees are not eligible for membership in the public service pension plan unless they meet the requirements to become a regular employee. Casual employees are not regular employees and are not members of the public service pension plan. The pension guide on this website does not apply to casual employees. You should refer the employee to his or her employer for pension information. What is a pension adjustment? A pension adjustment (PA) is a value that is attributed to your pension benefit in a particular year. The value of the pension adjustment is used by the Canada Revenue Agency to calculate your Registered Retirement Savings Plan (RRSP) contribution room for the following year. If you are a member of the public service pension plan, the PA is reported to you annually by the Government of Canada Pension Centre after you have reached 18 years of age and have accumulated two or more years of pensionable service. If you leave the public service before the end of the year in which you reach age 18, you will receive a PA in the year you leave. You can find this information on your annual Pension Statement of Benefits or on the Statement of Entitlement you receive when you cease employment in the public service. Pension statements are mailed in January to plan members who are employed on December 31 and retired members who are receiving a monthly public service pension. You can also access your pension statement and other pension-related information by registering for epension, the Government of Canada Pension Centre’s secure self-serve website. I have reviewed the public service pension guide and have additional questions. Who do I contact for more information? For more information about the public service pension plan, you may contact the Government of Canada Pension Centre. The Government of Canada Pension Centre can be reached through epension, the Government of Canada Pension Centre’s secure self-serve website. When you register for epension, you can use the online “Ask a Question” service to send a question to the Government of Canada Pension Centre by email. Your email address will appear automatically in the “To:” field. The Government of Canada Pension Centre will send you an email reply to your question within five business days.

Question: What is a pension adjustment and how is it calculated?
